independence_declaration.statement: domain-reviewer authored none of the DG7 candidate: no implementation, test, ADR, handover text, register row, release tool, drill, decision (D-242 to D-281) or stages.json change. I formed this verdict from my own runs in this session, on the frozen candidate and a disposable clone of it. I did not open any other reviewer's round-1 record or evidence, or any review record or reviewer evidence from the old branch's DG7 rounds. The old branch was used only for git objects (1612f85fc, 85f6ebe9f, 6f10ccc78, and the A26 run meta.json files) to check D-281's equivalence claim and the provenance of one protocol-audit hit.

checks_run.procedure: Verify the frozen candidate. Check the assignment's SHA-256. Recompute the candidate ID on the complete repository and diff it against the committed manifest. Confirm that HEAD differs from source_commit only in freeze metadata.
checks_run.command: sha256sum docs/delivery/assignments/DG7/round-1/domain-reviewer.md; git rev-parse HEAD; node tools/gates/candidate.mjs --stage DG7; node tools/gates/candidate.mjs --stage DG7 --diff docs/delivery/candidates/DG7/9822d8fe947b572d.manifest.json; git log --oneline ddf42ccd..HEAD; git diff --stat ddf42ccd HEAD
checks_run.environment: Repository /home/user/My-owns (complete clone, not shallow), Node 24.21.0 (/opt/nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin first on PATH), agent sandbox.
checks_run.expected: The assignment hash is f3e1e838…e99. The candidate ID is sha256:9822d8fe…a744 with 3158 files, and --diff matches. HEAD adds only freeze metadata on top of ddf42ccd.
checks_run.actual: The assignment hash matches. candidate_id sha256:9822d8fe947b572d30a24e1f59798587edd610a0c8b8f81a21eaceeb3233a744 with 3158 files, exit 0, and --diff gives matches: true with no added, removed or changed file (exit 0). HEAD is 2561ce969, the single freeze commit after ddf42ccd2. It adds only the three round-1 assignments and the manifest, and changes stages.json; all of these are excluded from the candidate. Two contradictions in the assignment, recorded rather than guessed. (1) It asks for 'round: 7', but the record directory is round-1, the stages.json round entry is round 1, and the validator (tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs l.682, l.794) requires rec.round to equal the directory round. This record therefore uses round 1. (2) The template it names, docs/delivery/reviews/DG5/round-7/domain-reviewer.json, does not exist (DG5 has rounds 1-5). I mirrored docs/delivery/reviews/DG6/round-7/domain-reviewer.json instead.

checks_run.procedure: Run historical validation of the approved gates DG1-DG6, the pipeline check and the current DG7 state. Run the gate-validator test suite, which holds the A23, A24 and F-DG0-121/211 tests the DG7 acceptance texts name. Check the register rules. Check P1-P7 stage order directly from stages.json.
checks_run.command: for s in DG1..DG6: node tools/gates/validate.mjs --historical --stage $s; node tools/gates/validate.mjs --pipeline; node tools/gates/validate.mjs --stage DG7; (clone) node --test tools/gates/tests/*.test.mjs; node tools/gates/validate.mjs --register DG7; node -e <stage-order script over stages.json>
checks_run.environment: Repository /home/user/My-owns (read-only validators), Node 24.21.0. The test suite ran in the disposable clone $TMPDIR/review-dg7 at ddf42ccd2.
checks_run.expected: DG1-DG6 historical PASS. --pipeline PASS with DG7 active. --stage DG7 non-zero only because the gate record does not exist yet. The validator tests all pass, including 'A23: a reviewer who authored the scope, or who is an owner, is rejected', 'A24: the pipeline cannot advance past a gate that is not APPROVED', 'the gate record must be written by the audited release-auditor invocation' and 'F-DG0-121 / F-DG0-211: the gate file must be what the auditor run wrote'. Register rules PASS. No stage shows BUILDING before the previous gate's APPROVED.
checks_run.actual: PASS gate DG1 to DG6 (historical), each exit 0. The first background run (historical-validate.txt) was stopped by the harness's 30-minute background limit while still in --pipeline. That was a time limit of my tool, not a validator failure, and its --pipeline and --stage DG7 sections are empty for that reason. The re-run (pipeline-validate.txt) gives 'PASS pipeline (active stage: DG7 REVIEWING)', exit 0. --stage DG7 exits 1 with exactly one problem, 'gate DG7: file not found (docs/delivery/gates/DG7.json)', which is expected before the audit. validator tests: 66 tests, 66 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped, 0 todo, exit 0. All four named tests pass. The only line matching 'skip' is the test name 'F-DG0-118: skip-worktree / assume-unchanged cannot hide edited evidence'. 'PASS register rules at DG7', exit 0. Stage order: every first BUILDING comes after the previous gate's last APPROVED, and DG7 BUILDING at 2026-11-12T12:02:49Z follows DG6 APPROVED at 11:30:26Z (stage-order.txt). REQ-DLV-005, 010, 021, 040, S20-023 and S20-028 keep their completes-after-gate clauses (the DG7 gate record, the audit and the seal), which this review cannot and does not supply.

checks_run.procedure: Judge D-281, which says the clean branch carries the product of 1612f85fc unchanged apart from listed exclusions. Diff 1612f85fc against ddf42ccd outside the D-281 exclusions. checks_run.procedure: Run the protocol audit myself on the frozen tree and compare its DG7 hits with the disclosures (D-249, D-269/D-270), the register notes of the J rows (REQ-DLV-008, 009, 011, 012, 018, 024, 027, 028) and known-limitations §2. checks_run.environment: Repository /home/user/My-owns (read-only; git history available, git-history=true), Node 24.21.0.
checks_run.expected: The audit exits 1 by design because of disclosed hits. For DG7, C1, C4, C6, C7, C8 and C9 PASS, and C2, C3 and C5 are exactly the D-270 disclosed hits. Every counted DG7 hit is disclosed, as known-limitations states.
checks_run.actual: Audit exit 1: 279 hits in 29 checks, 0 blocked, 36 pass. The hit set is identical to the orchestrator's protocol-audit-rg1.json. Non-zero exit explained: every DG0-DG6 hit is a D-249 H1-H11 disclosure. For DG7, C1, C4, C6, C7 and C9 PASS, and C8 (all stages) PASS. C3 has 7 hits (the five D-270 hits plus FE-C3 and DO-D8, as the REQ-DLV-012 note states). C5 has 1 hit (the late DG6 historical run, disclosed). C2 has 25 hits: 24 assignment-missing-elements (23 lacking only task/requirement ids, plus T-DG7-BE-A26) and 1 assignment-sha-mismatch for run DG7-T-DG7-ARCH-R6-…-a0fbc6f1, whose recorded assignment hash 37916ead… belongs to the 2026-11-14 version of T-DG7-ARCH-R6.md (85f6ebe9f). That version was overwritten on 2026-11-16 (6f10ccc78) for a second ARCH-R6 task, and the clean branch's single-commit history no longer contains it. All old-branch audits show 27 missing-element hits and no sha-mismatch. No record discloses this hit, while known-limitations §2 says the 25 DG7 C2 hits are 'disclosed by this release's records'. Raised as F-DG7-1001 (Medium, not mandatory).

checks_run.expected: All three scans PASS with exit 0. No stale allow-list entry. Every entry is bound to a value hash and explained as a fixture, a canary or a quoted record, not a credential.
checks_run.actual: Payload: 'PASS (payload; 3158 files; allowed 33; canary (documented) 22)', exit 0. History: 'PASS (history; 35931 files; allowed 219; canary (documented) 27)', exit 0, with no stale-entry line. This confirms on the frozen candidate that removing the two history-only entries (prefreeze-rg1 failed on exactly those two stale entries; prefreeze-rg1b passed) leaves the scan sound. Claims: 'PASS (891 files; D 141, U 750; negated 28; allowed 19)', exit 0. The allow-list has 44 entries. Each is rule plus path plus valueSha256, with reasons: synthetic test fixtures on loopback or .invalid hosts, a CI-only throwaway database password, ADR-0053 log-scan canaries, values quoted in approved delivery records (D-243 Q13), and the two history-only entries 42 and 43. None is a credential by its stated reason. The history scope is 'rev-list --objects HEAD' (secret-scan.mjs l.281), which is the shipped branch. Old-branch refs in this local repository are outside it by design.

checks_run.procedure: Check that the release notes are current, check the handover set, and judge their content. Unfinished items: every non-IMPLEMENTED row. Later clauses: every completes-after-gate row. External dependencies, the D-278 disclosure on every A5.6 surface, no approval claim, and G1-G6 kept apart from DG7. Compare ADR-0071 §5 with the generator.

checks_run.expected: --check is up to date and check-handover PASS. The release notes list 0 unfinished rows (all 412 rows are IMPLEMENTED), the 23 later clauses and the 11 external dependencies. They state 'engineering delivery states, not business approvals', mark Arabic as provisional, and carry the D-278 drill disclosure in the English and Arabic sections.
checks_run.actual: release-notes: '0 unfinished item(s), 23 later clause(s); … is up to date', exit 0. check-handover: PASS (index, deployment, summaries, security-links, guides, generated), exit 0. My protocol-audit report has the same hit set as the rg1 report (handover-checks.log), so known-limitations §2 is current for the frozen tree. Content: counts PLANNED 0, SPECIFIED 0, IMPLEMENTED 412, BLOCKED 0; 'None: every requirement of this release is implemented'. Each of the 23 later clauses names its remaining gate or seal clause, and REQ-DLV-021, 010 and S20-023 say no DG7 approval is granted or implied. All 11 dependencies are not_verified or not_configured, including corporate-idp, keycloak-e2e (one host, synthetic realm, not HA), live-ci and package-registry. The D-278 drill disclosure (A5.2 rule, engine ticks not covered, re-run the drill and never pause a job) is in known-limitations, deployment.md, both Arabic summaries and the release notes in both languages. Arabic is marked provisional (445 entries; arabic-review.json empty, disclosed). The D-270 hits appear in the release notes only by reference inside the later-clause entries; the full table is in known-limitations §2. I accept this, because D-270 names the register and release notes and both carry them. ADR-0071 §5.1 ('It reads nothing else') and §5.2 (seven sections) do not describe the extra input tools/release/release-notes-disclosures.json or the eighth section (D-280 accepted it without amending the ADR). Raised as F-DG7-1002 (Low, not mandatory, proposed for acceptance as an observation).

checks_run.procedure: Compare the handover user and admin guides (en and ar) and the in-app texts with the playbook: phases (B0021), gates G1-G6 (B0023), and value semantics (Unknown/Stale, Finance validation). Check that no text claims official PMI, certification, official Mobily branding, or a business, Finance, IT or production approval, and that product G6 is kept apart from DG7.
checks_run.command: read docs/handover/guides/user/en/user-guide.md (and ar), admin-guide; sed -n 83,107p docs/source/playbook.md; grep -i 'PMI|certif|official|brand|0078FF|complian' docs/handover/guides docs/handover/README.md docs/handover/operator-guide.md
checks_run.expected: Six phases Diagnose, Define, Design, Mobilize, Transform, Realize and gates G1 Case for Change … G6 Sustain as in B0021/B0023. Unknown and Stale are never zero or on track. Finance validation is the Finance role's in-product decision. The wordmark and colour are provisional. The playbook is 'inspired by' PMI, Brightline and BRM, not official or certified. A gate decision is not an IT, Finance or engineering approval, and G6 says nothing about the platform's release.
checks_run.actual: All as expected. The user guide's phase table and gate list match B0021/B0023 word for word (G1 Case for Change, G2 Direction, G3 Target State, G4 Mobilization, G5 Scale, G6 Sustain). Gate decisions need a mandatory rationale. KPIs without data show Unknown and stale data shows Stale, 'never … zero or on track', with text labels. Benefit formulas use decimal arithmetic and SAR by default. A Finance validation whose record changed shows 'Validation stale'. The guide states the brand colour and wordmark are provisional and not a verified Mobily brand, and that the playbook is 'inspired by PMI, Brightline and BRM … not an official PMI standard, and this product is not a certified product' (the Arabic guide says the same). 'Gate G6 says nothing about the platform's own delivery or release.' Sample data is labelled synthetic. The claims scan (DOM-RG1-04) passes. The guides do not explain RAG-from-trajectory or the separate delivery, adoption, value and closure states in detail. That is a summary choice of a handover guide, not a contradiction of the playbook, and the in-product screens were reviewed at earlier gates.

checks_run.procedure: Review, without re-running it, the orchestrator's container host evidence (D-267). No Docker daemon is available in this sandbox, so this check is a review of the logs and does not claim the container run as my own. I read every step's command and exit, the /readyz body, the no-egress smoke, the Keycloak e2e runs and the image save/rm/load, and I compared the claims in REQ-S01-001, S01-006, S16-008, S19-010, S19-018 and S20-018 with the logs. The environmental residuals (live registry D-057, live CI D-058, real IdP D-049, external systems, capacity) are judged on the offline and config surface, as the assignment directs.
checks_run.command: grep '### NN $|exit=' docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG7/orchestrator/host/host-run.log, host-run-3b.log, host-run-3c.log; read the no-egress-stack.log and keycloak-e2e-stack.log warnings
checks_run.environment: Repository /home/user/My-owns (read-only logs). The container commands themselves are not re-run (no Docker daemon in agent sandboxes, D-243 Q1).
checks_run.expected: Build, save, rm, load and verify exit 0. 'compose up --pull never --wait' reaches /readyz ready with database, storage and worker reported. The no-egress stack is healthy and its smoke passes with outbound connections refused. Keycloak e2e 4/4. Every failure in the logs is explained.
checks_run.actual: host-run.log steps 00-10 exit 0. Step 07: /readyz {status: ready, checks: {database ok, migrations ok, storage ok, worker alive}}, exit 0. Step 11 (Keycloak e2e) exit 1, 4 failed. In host-run-3b, b07 exit 1 with 4 failed again, while b01-b03 pass: the no-egress stack is healthy and the smoke is 15/15, including 'no outbound internet: … tcp 1.1.1.1:443 ENETUNREACH; dns registry.npmjs.org EAI_AGAIN'. host-run-3c b07, with the proxy variables unset, gives 4 passed, exit 0. The two failed Keycloak runs are explained by D-267 and ADR-0069 Amendment 2: the test process inherited the sandbox proxy, which cannot reach the local container. Both are kept, not hidden. The 'unexpected "iss" (issuer)' warnings in keycloak-e2e-stack.log come from the foreign-realm negative test, which expects the API to reject another issuer. The postgres line 'logical replication launcher … exited with exit code 1' is the normal stop of the temporary server during initdb. Residuals I accept as disclosed: one host with registry access through a proxy (not air-gapped; 'host without registry access' as ADR-0069 §6 defines it: images removed, loaded from the bundle, then --pull never, residual 5); not HA; the host run used the D-267 integration tree, not this frozen candidate (D-243 Q1 makes it orchestrator evidence for reviewers to judge). The offline lifecycle e2e (DO-E offline drill run 2) and the T-B11 drill cover the later trees. My result is PASS for the evidence review: the logs show what the register claims. I make no claim to have run the container half myself.
